lines: A wage plate wedged in the cliff: 'Ruskweber pays. Ruskweber collects.'
You take a rubbing of the plate.
A tonic was stuck behind it. Finders keepers.
Just a bare patch where a plate used to be.
A wage plate under the platform: 'Late is a cost. Sorry is a cost.'
You take a rubbing of the plate.
A tonic was stuck behind it. Finders keepers.
Just a bare patch where a plate used to be.
A wage plate nailed behind the archive shelves: 'Paid in full. Signed, nobody.'
You take a rubbing of the plate.
A tonic was stuck behind it. Finders keepers.
Just a bare patch where a plate used to be.
A press platen behind the station stove, still in Gorse's wrapping paper.
Only soot left back here.
Archivist Brisk: All eight wage plates. Fifty years of the clan's payroll, and every week a little crueller.
Archivist Brisk: I'll hang them in the hall. Nothing frightens a clan like its own receipts.
Archivist Brisk: The plates are up. Three clan men came to look. One cried. Good.

brisk_ask: Archivist Brisk: The Ruskweber clan stamped its wages on brass plates, then hid them. Eight of them.
Archivist Brisk: Two are up here somewhere, six down in the Soot Vaults. Bring me rubbings of all of them.

lines: Census Man Mott: I count Spirlings for the clan tax. Six kinds live down in the Vaults, and nobody's paid on them in years.
Census Man Mott: Bring each one past me. Don't worry, I only tax the ones that can't run.
Census Man Mott: You're all counted. I put you down as a dependant. Of the clan.
Census Man Mott: A Hushkin. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: A Blotling. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: A Duskdigger. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: A Calderox. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: A Cairnhold. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: A Talusgard. Counted. Taxed. Welcome to the books.
Census Man Mott: That's all six. The clan owes you a receipt. Here's mine instead.

mott_more: Census Man Mott: Still missing some. The Vaults are full of them. Mind the guards, they bill by the hour.

lines: Foreman Gorse: Halvard's old hand press is missing three parts. Thieves, the lot of 'em.
Foreman Gorse: One by the station, the rest down in the Vaults, I'd bet. Find 'em and I'll put in a good word.
Foreman Gorse: Any luck with them parts?
Every part came wrapped in a pawn ticket with Gorse's name on it.
Foreman Gorse: Ah. Well. A man's got debts. Halvard's got a press. It was simple maths.
Foreman Gorse: Tell you what. You forget the tickets, I forget your face. No? Then let's do this the loud way.

gorse_more: Foreman Gorse: Keep looking. And if anyone asks, I was never here.
gorse_after: Foreman Gorse: Halvard put me on sweeping duty. For life. It's very clean down here now.

lines: Foreman Gorse: Fine! Take the parts to Halvard. I'll tell him I found them. He won't believe me either.
Kiln-Keeper Tovan: The old town kiln went cold the day the clan stopped paying for coal.
Your Ember Spirling breathes on the grate. The kiln coughs, then roars.
Kiln-Keeper Tovan: Ha! Free heat. Don't tell the clan, they'll send a bill for the warmth.

tovan_need: Kiln-Keeper Tovan: Got an Ember Spirling? Bring one in your team. A spark's all it needs.
tovan_after: Kiln-Keeper Tovan: She's burning lovely. The clan already sent a man to ask about it. I said 'what kiln'.

lines: Engraver Pell: I'm cutting a plate for the old Wardens. The guild says it needs ash from three places in the Vaults.
Engraver Pell: Superstition, mostly. But the last plate without it fell on a man. A clan man. So, mixed results.
Engraver Pell: Three ashes. Lovely. The Wardens get their plate, the clan gets nothing. My favourite kind of job.
Engraver Pell: The plate's up. Every name spelled right, for once.

pell_more: Engraver Pell: Still need ash. Wage cellar, kiln drains and the strongroom, if you dare.

lines: Tibb: My Mirkmole ran into the Vaults under Cinderfold. Get him back? Please? I'm only small.
Tibb: Mole! You found him! ...Oh. And you didn't open the chest he was sleeping in? Shame.
Tibb: My brother Dace said a mug would carry the chest out too. Dace! The mug's back!
Tibb: Mole's in the Vaults. Deep. Probably asleep on something shiny.
Tibb: No hard feelings. Uncle Fitch says you're alright now. That's rare.
Dace: Ugh. Fine. Kid keeps the mole, you keep your teeth. Fair trade in Ashmere.
Tibb: I'll tell Uncle Fitch you're family-ish. He runs the toll in the Vaults.
Warden Harl: Bring an old man coal from the Vaults and he'll tell you how Ashmere really works. One sack, one story.
Warden Harl: Story one. The first Paymaster paid in bread. People liked him. So the clan replaced him.
Warden Harl: Story two. I kept the Kiln Rift for thirty years. The clan sent me a medal. Then a bill for the medal.
Warden Harl: Story three. My best friend sold my post to the Ruskwebers. I'd have done the same. That's the sad part.
Warden Harl: That's all my stories. The moral is: count your fingers after every handshake.

harl_more: Warden Harl: No coal, no story. I'm old, not charitable.

lines: Bram: Came all the way from Crowcrest. My Shalebats flew off over the ash. Three of them.
Bram: My cousin Rook lives here. He said he'd keep an eye out. Good lad, Rook.
Bram: My bats! Where were they? ...A cage in the Vaults? With Rook's name on the tag?
Rook: Cousin! Funny story. Actually it's not funny. Your friend here is about to have a bad day.
Bram: Rook hasn't seen them. Says the Vaults are no place for bats. Odd thing to say.
Bram: Family. You can't choose 'em, but you can stop lending 'em money.
Rook: The Paymaster paid good money for bats! Times are hard, cousin!
Bram: Then get a job, Rook. Here, this is for you. Not you, Rook.
Widow Marn: The clan wrote IOUs to half this town and hid them in the Vaults. Five of them. Bring them up and I'll burn them, free folk at last.
Widow Marn: All five. You didn't read the names on them, did you? 'Owed to Marn.' Every one.
Widow Marn: Burn them? Darling, I'm going to frame them. Here's your cut. Don't spend it on trust.
Widow Marn: Collections are up this week. Thank you for your service.

marn_more: Widow Marn: Five IOUs, darling. Every room of the Vaults has one tucked somewhere.

lines: The verse scratched here reads: 'Salt keeps the dead and the debts the same.'
You know this verse by heart now.
The verse scratched here reads: 'Glass remembers every face that lied to it.'
You know this verse by heart now.
The verse scratched here reads: 'Sing it once for free. Twice costs extra.'
You know this verse by heart now.
Busker Wenna: The salt flats had a song once. Three verses, scratched into the Vault walls so the clan couldn't tax the paper.
Busker Wenna: That's the whole song! Listen.
Busker Wenna: ...Yeah, it's worse sung. Most true things are. Have this, I can't afford to keep it.
Busker Wenna: The clan fined me for singing it. Worth every coin you didn't give me.

wenna_more: Busker Wenna: Three verses on three walls down in the Soot Vaults. Look closely.
juno_1_intro: Juno: You're after the wage plates too? Cute. I'm Juno Sallow. I collect things. Mostly other people's.
juno_1_defeat: Juno: Alright, you've got hands. Saltglass next. Don't be late, I hate waiting for losers.
juno_1: Juno: Alright, you've got hands. Saltglass next. Don't be late, I hate waiting for losers.
juno_2_intro: Juno: Second round. I've been training. Also lying. Mostly training.
juno_2_defeat: Juno: Again? Fine. Last plate's in the Vaults strongroom. See you at the bottom, rookie.
juno_2: Juno: Again? Fine. Last plate's in the Vaults strongroom. See you at the bottom, rookie.
